newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus regrets U.S. arrogance in Boeing talks.
newsitem.headline: Airbus regrets U.S. arrogance in Boeing talks.

text.p: Airbus Industrie on Wednesday said it regretted the "arrogant and confrontational" attitude of the United States in talks with the European Union on the planned merger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp.

The European Commission on Wednesday said it had decided in principle to approve the $15 billion aerospace merger after Boeing had offered some concessions on Tuesday, removing the main obstacle to the deal.
The formal decision will be made in a week's time, Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert told a news conference.

"Airbus Industrie takes note of the Commission's decision but has no immediate comment to make because it has no knowledge of the last-minute concessions made by Boeing to counter the Commission's objections to the merger," Airbus spokesman Alain Dupeich told Reuters by telephone from Toulouse in south-west France.
"Airbus Industrie regrets, however, the arrogant and confrontational attitude of the U.S.A. in these discussions," he added.
"The unnecessary tension could have been avoided had Boeing proposed true remedies to contentious points raised by the Commission at the outset of the talks," Dupiech said.

Financial analysts and industry executives said that the Boeing/McDonnell merger could be a blessing in disguise for Airbus as it would put further pressure on industry and governments to turn the consortium into a real company.
They also said that the Boeing concession to renounce three exclusive supply deals with U.S. airlines and its promise not to seek new exclusive deals for 10 years, was less important than it seemed.
Boeing dropped exclusive supply contracts with AMR Corp's American Airlines, Continental Airlines and Delta Air Lines.

"The fact is that in the civil aircraft industry you buy an airliner for 25 years. You have massive investment and you get massive economies from single types," Chris Avery, aerospace analyst at Paribas in London, told Reuters Financial Television.
"The economic effect of these deals will continue even if the terms get dropped from the contracts," he added.
An analyst at a Paris-based brokerage said on the contrary the exclusivity deal was important.

"The exclusive contracts were the big worry to me," he said. "With the exclusive supply contracts Airbus would have virtually been kept off the U.S. market. Now they stand to win orders there, as they have shown in the past they can."
German Foreign Affairs Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Wednesday morning that Europe must now focus on strengthening Airbus in response to the merger.
"The aerospace industry in Europe has seen no consolidation at all by comparison with the massive moves that have taken place in the U.S.A. in the last four years," Paribas' Avery said.
"The single most important thing that would help Airbus to gain market share against Boeing is to reform itself and become more competitive.

"To have competitive sub-contract pricing rather than fixed-price work shares. Moves like that would be far much more important for Airbus to gain market share on Boeing than any conditions attached to the acquisition of McDonnell Douglas," Avery said.

A French analyst said airlines would prefer to keep a balance between the two suppliers and the balance of power would "almost mechanically" switch from the current 65/35 to 55/45 in favour of Boeing.
In 1996, Boeing obtained 66 percent of new aircraft orders, McDonnell four percent and Airbus 30 percent.
"Airlines would not want to see that Boeing gets too much market power. It is in their interest to have Airbus as a counter balance," said an executive of a French aerospace supplier.

Toulouse-based Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Societe Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.

The four companies and the governments of the member countries have agreed that Airbus should become a proper company with its own balance sheet and results. However the companies still disagree about which assets to transfer to Airbus, and at what price.
